sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

Case M24: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 280x280x330 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case M24 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(280, 280, 330) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: myxoid soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 165/330 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: The image looks too dark, so I'll try adjusting the sheets instead.

content.text: sheet axial 60–300/330 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm noticing a large mass on axial slice 147 with two distinct lobes - an anterior-left component and a brighter posterior-medial one, while slice 191 shows it as a single unified mass. I want to look more closely at slice 147.

content.text: axial 150/330 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15
axial 205/330 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
At slice 205 I'm seeing one large homogeneous mass in the anterior thigh, while at 150 it splits into two lobes - a darker anterior-right lobe and a brighter central one. I'm trying to figure out which lobe represents the actual tumor versus surrounding tissue, since the mass seems to span roughly z=120 to 250.

I suspect that darker anterior-right lobe might just be a compressed muscle like the vastus rather than tumor, so I should check the coronal and sagittal views to clarify.

content.text: sheet coronal 80–200/280 (8 slices) | v0 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm examining the coronal slices around index 114, noting the mass appears to have two components - an upper darker region and a brighter lower-right portion. I want to compare this more closely with coronal slice 125 using annotated marks.

content.text: coronal 118/280 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: This is tricky given the low contrast—the mass spans a wide range of slices and seems lobulated, with one lobe appearing brighter at certain levels than the other, though brightness looks more uniform elsewhere. I'll try running seg_point on that brighter lobe to see what gets captured.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 470.0 mL | components 7 (largest 99.9%; 6 others total 0.0 mL) | extent axial 21–261, coronal 86–162, sagittal 106–193 | change +470.0 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 170, coronal 122, sagittal 148 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
The segmentation captured the whole mass including both lobes, but there's a leaky tail extending inferiorly to z~21 that needs cleanup. I should apply a morphological opening to strip the thin tail and keep only the largest connected component, then double-check whether both lobes are genuinely tumor by reviewing axial slice 170.

I'm uncertain about the darker versus brighter lobe distinction — this could be the thigh/knee region, with the dark posterior crescent possibly representing muscle (hamstring) rather than tumor. Given the heterogeneous signal typical of a lobulated myxoid tumor, I'm inclined to include both lobes, but I want to verify by examining additional axial slices (130, 135, 140, 205, 235) and the sagittal view to confirm the structure before finalizing the mask.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 441.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 83–254, coronal 86–156, sagittal 106–193 | change +0.0 mL / -28.3 mL | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15 | edit open | image: axial 174, coronal 122, sagittal 148 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I want to confirm whether that right lobe region is actually tumor, so I'm checking different axial slices with the mask overlaid, looking at slices 130 and 240 with the cropped mask view.

content.text: axial 130/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15
axial 240/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial 130, I notice the right-anterior lobe looks like a separate, muscle-like elongated structure, lighter in tone and divided from the bright lobe by a dark line—possibly displaced vastus lateralis muscle or part of the tumor itself. Comparing it to the darker muscle lobe on the left side at the same level, versus the homogeneous appearance at slice 205, makes me want to pin down exactly which tissue this represents.

There seems to be a faint cleft between structures around 170/174, and a subtler seam near 165-170 on the 205 slice, which could mean the tumor sits deep to the muscle in an oval shape with a slight indentation. At slice 150 the right lobe reads brighter than the surrounding muscle, but the overall contrast is too low for me to be confident without being able to adjust the window—I think I need to zoom into the mask crop around slice 165 to get a clearer read.

content.text: axial 165/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay none | v2 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15
axial 195/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay none | v2 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At slice 165, the bright central lobe shows a heterogeneous pinwheel pattern suggestive of myxoid tumor, distinct from the anterior muscle which is separated by a dark fat plane. By slice 195 everything merges into one mass, with the tumor seeming to abut the vastus muscle at lower levels while expanding more superiorly.

I'm trying to track whether the right-anterior crescent at 165 is compressed muscle wrapping around the tumor, or if at 195 the whole oval becomes indistinguishable tumor tissue. Cross-referencing coronal 118 and sagittal 148 views, I'm still finding the boundary between tumor and muscle genuinely ambiguous, particularly around the posterior cleft at slice 195 where brightness patterns seem continuous with the bright lobe seen at 165.

Looking at coronal 118, I see an upper darker homogeneous block and a lower brighter block that could represent muscle versus tumor, though the sagittal view shows a more uniform oval shape with only a subtle brighter region posteriorly. Given the overall size and appearance, this is most consistent with a large myxoid soft-tissue sarcoma spanning the whole mass rather than separate muscle and tumor compartments.

The brightness differences could just reflect coil intensity falloff rather than a true internal boundary — the upper block's dimness near the edge of the field matches what I'd expect from signal dropoff rather than distinct tissue. I want to check more coronal and sagittal slices across the mask range to see if there's a genuine internal divide or if this is one continuous myxoid tumor.

content.text: sheet sagittal 110–190/280 (8 slices) | v2 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking across the sagittal slices, the mass appears as a coherent ovoid with a brighter posterior region and dimmer anterior region, and the mask extends further inferiorly posteriorly. I'm leaning toward treating the whole heterogeneous ovoid, bright and dark areas together, as a single myxoid tumor with a heterogeneous periphery rather than splitting it into separate components.

Trying to track the right-sided lobe across axial and sagittal views to figure out whether it's a distinct muscle structure or part of the mass itself—measuring its craniocaudal extent (roughly 130mm, spanning most of the full height) suggests it's too compact to be a long muscle like vastus, more consistent with it being an ovoid mass component rather than a separate anatomical structure cut off by the field of view.

I'm now checking the mask boundaries more carefully across slices—looking at the inferior extent in coronal views, a notch and tail-like extension in sagittal 156, and a small spike at the top. I want to pull up additional coronal slices with the outline overlaid to verify nothing was missed at these edges.

content.text: coronal 135/280 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15
sagittal 156/280 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: I notice a hole in the mask at the notch between the lobes that filling holes could address, and I'm also checking whether the mask correctly tracks the inferior tail of the bright lobe extending down toward the bottom of the slice.

content.text: sheet axial 84–126/330 (6 slices) | v2 | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: Slices 92 and 101 look like thin, plausible partial-volume tapering of the tumor, so I'll keep them mostly as-is, maybe trimming minor bits below slice 95. Now I'll fill holes in the mask and move on to checking the upper boundary and reviewing segmentation candidates.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 441.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 83–254, coronal 86–156, sagittal 106–193 | change none | tool calls 17/40, prompts 1/15 | edit fill_holes | image: axial 174, coronal 122, sagittal 148 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: Fill_holes didn't change anything since the 3D hole wasn't enclosed, but the mask still looks fine, so I'll check the upper end and review candidates through seg_finish.

content.text:
Final review of v3: volume 441.6 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 83–254, coronal 86–156, sagittal 106–193 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 1/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 227 mL, touches mask on its anterior, posterior and left sides, mostly inferior of the mask
C2 add 159 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C3 add 78 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly superior of the mask
C4 add 24 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
C5 add 0.6 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "2647" to save it.

content.thinking: These candidates all look like normal tissue or skin, so I'll reject them. The mask looks good, so I'll finish with medium confidence.

arguments.reason: Mask covers the whole ovoid T2-intermediate/bright mass with smooth boundary in all planes; the candidates were skin or muscle, so I rejected them. It is uncertain whether the anterior-right lobe is tumor or displaced muscle, and I included it.

content.text: case M24 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v3 | final volume 441.6 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 19/40, prompts 1/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I saved the mask for case M24 (version v3): one connected component of 441.6 mL, with medium confidence.

- **Method:** one positive point on the large mass was enough to capture it. I then applied a 5 mm morphological opening to cut off thin inferior leaks, and a hole-fill that changed nothing.
- **Fit:** the outline follows the ovoid mass in all three planes. It spans axial slices 83–254, and the end slices just past it show no tumor tissue.
- **Rejected candidates:** all five automatic proposals were skin, subcutaneous fat or muscle next to the mass, so I did not accept any.
- **Main uncertainty:** the anterior-right lobe looks like a separate crescent at some levels (around axial 130–165). I kept it as tumor because it has rounded ends and merges with the mass higher up. If it is displaced muscle, the mask is too large by that lobe.
- **Thin inferior tail:** the mask tapers into a thin, dim tail in the lowest slices (about axial 85–105). I left it in; it may be partial-volume tail rather than tumor.
